scope: Theorem 5.4 (Single-exponential recovery) of the manuscript “Single-exponential recovery and bounded-price strictness for metric k-median” (preprints/Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-Price-Strictness-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 823fdb284a7d3c0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose |S| = |O| = h ≥ 1, P = cost(O) > 0, and O has an injective proxy map into S for its good centers such that X i good X p∈Ci d(p, ϕi) ≤ Pg + 0.01P. Assume the number m of bad centers is at most a supplied bound M0. On the positive bounded integral instances used in the body of the proof, for every 0 < ζ < 1 an algorithm knowing only S, M0, ζ returns a real solution of size at most h and cost at most 1.97P with probability at least 1 − ζ. Its running time is exp(O(M0)) poly(N) log(2/ζ). In particular this is polynomial time for every fixed constant in M0 = O(log N). Local optimality of S is not an additional hypothesis of this theorem.
